All pointers below are at treams-rs revision fcf62400700e326ffcc61ec50025cb25ea43ea6d, verified HEAD during investigation. Working pyproject.toml/uv.lock changes were ignored. Findings are source-confirmed; no probes/tests executed.

  • A constructor dispatch boundary can reuse existing adapters. Each adapter binds the same _framework.Constructors and _framework.Operations to its backend (python/treams_rs/_framework.py:62–95, jax.py:184–209, torch.py:179–204). The framework objects retain _backend and dispatch their subsequent numerical operations through it (_framework_tmatrix.py:59–84). Sphere construction already collects material fields using framework arrays, executes a native record, and returns framework TMatrix (_framework.py:261–292). No new derivative implementation is necessary.

  • Dispatching only the differentiable constructor is insufficient for the ordinary physics workflow. With sphere = tr.sphere_tmatrix(radius=tracer, ...), a separate all-constant tr.plane_wave(...) would still produce the ordinary NumPy class. Framework _regular_incident calls incident.in_basis(..., positions=..., singular=False) (_framework_tmatrix.py:23–30), but ordinary PlaneWave.in_basis accepts only basis (_waves.py:423–426). This fails before scattering. Existing docs accordingly require every object to be created in the adapter namespace (docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:99–102). A useful transparent scope must explicitly handle NumPy constant physics objects at composition boundaries; otherwise offer one backend-bound namespace/context so every constructor selects consistently. Do not claim input dispatch alone completes ordinary API compatibility.

  • Materials are another early boundary. Framework Material is a frozen dataclass retaining values (_framework_backend.py:45–51); as_material accepts that class, ordinary Material, a tuple, or epsilon alone (54–65). Ordinary Material is usable only after its fields have survived construction; promotion cannot restore a discarded gradient. Initial scope can support direct epsilon/tuples and dispatch ordinary Material before coercion, rather than general object traversal. Nested material lists are already individually converted (_framework.py:273–278). PyTorch explicitly recursively stacks list/tuple tensors to avoid detachment (torch.py:166–176).

Smallest useful scope: selected module-level physical constructors, initially sphere/multilayer sphere plus plane wave and their existing scattering/field methods; reuse existing framework classes. Treat ordinary Python/NumPy values as NumPy unless a supported backend input or explicit choice exists. Do not alter class identity via TMatrix.__new__, retrofit all root methods, or claim arbitrary NumPy code support. To make the realistic example below work with only import treams_rs as tr, either (a) narrowly promote a NumPy incident plane wave when a framework response consumes it, or (b) expose one explicit backend-bound API and consistently construct through it. Option (b) is the smaller coherent first change if fully transparent constants would broaden scope.

Existing documented equivalent, runnable with installed Advect adapter:

import advect
import treams_rs.advect as tr

def scattering(radius):
    sphere = tr.sphere_tmatrix(k0=1.3, lmax=2, radius=radius, material=3)
    incident = tr.plane_wave([0, 0, 1], "positive_helicity", k0=1.3)
    return sphere.cross_sections(incident).scattering

value, derivative = advect.value_and_grad(scattering)(
    advect.numpy.asarray(0.2)
)

Exact existing example: docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:14–26. JAX version uses jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) and jax.jit(jax.value_and_grad(scattering))(0.2) (31–45); PyTorch uses CPU float64 scalar requires_grad=True, then .backward() (50–59). Changing only the import to root treams_rs is a proposal, contingent on the constant-composition change above.

Current limits, preserved by dispatch:

Adapter Supported contract Limits/source
Advect CPU first-order reverse mode; float32/64 and complex64/128 inputs; outputs double precision; input-dtype gradients No higher order, JVP, staging or checkpoint; docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:68–76
JAX CPU float64/complex128 with x64 enabled; grad/VJP, JIT, checkpoint, sequential vmap _inputs enforces default CPU/device/dtype (jax.py:59–75). custom_vjp + pure_callback, backward recomputes forward (78–120). No higher derivatives/JVP. Return arrays across JIT, not physics objects: not registered pytrees (docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:99–102).
PyTorch CPU float64/complex128; eager backward/autograd.grad; repeated backward with retain_graph CPU/dtype checks (torch.py:100–107); first backward consumes saved native pullback, later backward rerecords (80–97). Higher order explicitly rejected (83–86). Forward mode, torch.func and torch.compile unsupported (1–23); transparent selection does not change this.

Output and cotangent contract must remain unchanged: records return one scalar/array or a flat tuple plus context/pullback; outputs become float64/complex128 (_records.py:75–96). Pullback returns one gradient per dynamic input, matching shape/dtype; real inputs take real gradient parts (99–152). Rust uses Re(vdot(g, dx)); Advect and Torch use it directly, JAX conjugates incoming cotangents and outgoing gradients (_records.py:115–117, jax.py:108–114, torch.py:94–97). Preserve context lifetime and repeated-backward behavior.

Existing validation anchors for later change:

  • JAX JIT/vmap/checkpoint and repeated VJP: tests/autodiff/test_jax.py:30–41; precision/shape/higher-order rejection: 45–56.
  • PyTorch conjugate/noncontiguous views: tests/autodiff/test_torch.py:23–38; repeated backward and native call count: 41–65; composed field objective: 68–75; NumPy constant mutation: 78–89; mutation/higher-order errors: 92–101.
  • Cross-framework scalar value/gradient harness JITs JAX objectives: tests/autodiff/test_framework_physics.py:48–60. Physics identities for sphere/cylinder scattering scaling and lossless absorption: 558–579.
  • Native bridge complex-convention checks: tests/autodiff/test_adapter_bridges.py:316–319.

Additional narrowly targeted validation should compare proposed root dispatch against these existing adapters for radius, frequency and material gradients; test constant incident objects and nested materials; reject mixed backends before coercion; verify no optional framework imports during plain NumPy import/calls; measure ordinary NumPy call overhead and preserve root result types.

items.html:
Completed shared physics promotion and composition.

  • Constants promote into the selected backend; mixed backends reject before coercion.
  • Added plane-wave polarization parity, Cartesian amplitudes, numeric scalar labels, and differentiable real directions off-axis.
  • Concrete Torch/JAX directions retain automatic incident-side selection.
  • Added plane-port expansion, batched field sampling, root r= field keywords, metadata aliases, and identical-basis wave preservation.
  • Reused existing native derivatives throughout.

Verified: 100 focused tests, 201 namespace tests, shared vocabulary test, Ruff, Pyrefly, and whitespace checks. All four backends tested; JAX gradients ran under JIT.

Remaining limits: direction derivatives at polarization axes remain undefined; differentiable directions require explicit incident side for planar power. No commits or release-worktree changes.
